t: A small appanage on the Moskva River that rose under Alexander Nevsky's descendants to unite north-eastern Russia.
Its princes grew rich and powerful as tribute collectors for the Golden Horde, then ended Tatar overlordship in 1480.
Ivan III annexed Novgorod and Tver and rebuilt the Kremlin; in 1547 Ivan IV was crowned tsar and Muscovy became Russia.
dyk: Ivan I's nickname Kalita means 'money bag' or 'purse', probably a reference to the wealth he amassed or to his reputed alms-giving.
ev: Daniel, son of Alexander Nevsky, receives Moscow as his principality
Ivan I Kalita becomes sole grand prince of Vladimir
Dmitry Donskoy defeats Mamai at the Battle of Kulikovo
Khan Tokhtamysh takes and burns Moscow
Ivan III annexes the Novgorod Republic
The Great Stand on the Ugra River ends Tatar overlordship
Ivan III issues the Sudebnik law code
Ivan IV is crowned tsar, founding the Tsardom of Russia
